reconcile.note: John Gill argues both animals were brought and dressed with garments, so Matthew's them need not mean Jesus rode both at once, unlike Mark and Luke's single colt.

discrepancy.note: Strauss argues Matthew's statement that Jesus required and sat on two donkeys at once is the most striking, unparalleled feature of the entry narrative.

quotes.text: The most striking part of this account is obviously the statement of Matthew, that Jesus not only required two asses, though he alone intended to ride, but that he also actually sat on them both.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), ch. on the entry into Jerusalem, on Matthew 21:7.

sides.snippet: brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them
sides.verseText: and brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.

sides.snippet: threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it
sides.verseText: They brought the young donkey to Jesus, and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.
